text:
Ibrahim: sketching an approach we discussed offline: regional shared NAT/backing-relay with a fast "sticky-IP" handoff for customers who need source-ip stability. want to capture failure modes and mitigation ideas.
Yuki: high level: prefer shared infra by default, reserve stable ips for enterprise via lease tokens. biggest technical problem is long-lived TCP/gRPC sessions during IP handoff.
Taylor: agreed. we could pre-warm the new host: replicate TCP 4-tuple mapping and prime neighbor/arp tables before flipping the lease. trick is to ensure symmetric routing for in-flight packets.
Rohit: how do we prime symmetric routing across cloud infra? we can advertise the floating IP on the new host then ARP-probe the subnet. ALB/NAT tables might still route to old host until BGP/ARP converges. need a short drain window.
Ibrahim: proposed handoff sequence: 1) allocate target host, 2) replicate socket metadata (best-effort), 3) advertise IP on target and start hairpin/bounce proxy for ~2s, 4) switch forwarding rules. aim to keep disruption <5s.
Yuki: we should accept that some edge cases will get a reset (mobile clients with NATs). Document SLO: for request/response flows 99% <2s, for long-lived streams recommend ENI/dedicated shard.
Taylor: alternative: use an application-layer proxy that terminates connection at relay and multiplexes to backend via stable internal channel. That avoids source-ip flip but forces termination at our layer and breaks customer private cert constraints.
Rohit: can we do TLS passthrough + a small TCP-proxy shim that preserves TLS but proxies packets until handoff completes? essentially a TCP splice that hands socket ownership. kernel-level splice exists but is brittle across kernels. avoid kernel modules.
Ibrahim: another mitigation is to prefer QUIC/UDP for internal relays where possible; QUIC handles connection migration better. but many customers use gRPC over HTTP/2/TCP. this should be in migration docs.
Yuki: monitoring requirements: track per-lease handshake latency, handoff attempts, percent of sessions reset during handoff, and per-tenant long-lived session fraction. flag tenants with >5% resets during handoffs.
Taylor: ops/runbook: if handoff failure spike observed, auto-roll back leases to ENI-assigned tenants and open an incident. include manual commands to flush ARP and re-bind ip on ENI.
Rohit: security: leases must be cryptographically authorized (signed tokens) and auditable. record every lease allocation & handoff event in immutable log with tenant id, host id, seq.
net-bot: scheduled test run: sticky-lease-handoff-2026-03-23 (ETA 40m) :satellite:
Ibrahim: open questions to include in RFC follow-up:
- exact pre-warm protocol for socket priming (what metadata to replicate)
- limits for number of sticky leases per host and failure isolation rules
- deterministic backoff strategy when ARP convergence delays exceed threshold
- pricing model & enterprise SLA language for pinned-ip offering
Yuki: I'll draft the RFC appendix with monitoring indicators and SLOs. Taylor: can you prototype the bounce-proxy idea in user-space? Rohit: you own the security appendix and token format.
Taylor: will mock a tiny userspace splice; will post perf numbers.
Rohit: will propose a signed JWT format for lease tokens and include revocation semantics.
Ibrahim: thanks. let's keep the assumption that long-lived RPCs > 30m default to ENI unless tenant opts into best-effort sticky leases. post RFC link here when ready.
Yuki: :thumbsup:
